Today’s failing approach: client submissions based on resumes and ad hoc tests
Unverified resume claims
A technology listed on a resume does not demonstrate the candidate’s ability to use it in a client project.
Different assessment criteria
A take-home exercise and an informal phone screen can leave you with results that are difficult to compare.
Unclear authorship
A completed submission alone may not give your reviewer enough evidence to evaluate the candidate’s contribution.
Incomplete submission evidence
If your recruiter cannot explain the technical result, the client may need to repeat the assessment.

Codility Screen is an asynchronous technical assessment platform. Your recruiter chooses a set of tasks relevant to the client’s role, and the candidate completes the task in a realistic environment.
Your team reviews the assessment evidence before deciding whether to submit the candidate. That matters even more for staffing agencies than a direct employer.

Match the assessment to the client’s technology
Codility’s library includes more than 1,300 validated engineering tasks. Paste in the client’s job description and AI recommends the best-matched tasks for the role. Selected tasks score automatically against defined test cases, helping your team review results without arranging an engineer-led screen for every candidate.
You can create a custom task with AI (via MCP) or discuss bespoke development from Codility’s team of assessment scientists
The difference:
Your recruiter can assess candidates against a task related to the client’s role.
Review the output behind the score
The candidate record includes the submitted code and per-test-case results. Deterministic scoring means the same submission earns the same score.
Codility provides validation documentation for review and supports customer-specific adverse impact analysis through Professional Services. Your recruitment team can use the record to explain its own submission decision.
Your reviewer can check the technical evidence before recommending a candidate.

Investigate integrity concerns before submitting a candidate
Codility combines behavioral, similarity, identity and network signals into a reviewable integrity risk level. Your reviewer can inspect the contributing signals and the code evolution timeline.
An integrity signal requires review. Your team makes the decision about the result and any follow-up with the candidate.
Your reviewer can investigate a concern before the client begins its own evaluation.
Consider the experience of candidates you may contact again
Codility research found that 91% of candidates considered the content fair and 87% rated the assessment experience good or excellent.

Frequently asked questions
Codility Screen provides task-based engineering assessments with submitted code, scoring detail and integrity evidence. Confirm the account setup and permissions required for your agency’s client-submission process before choosing a configuration.
Technical staffing partners can combine resume reviews, recruiter calls and technical exercises. A standardized work-sample assessment can give your reviewers comparable evidence for candidates applying to the same client role.
The candidate report provides an assessment result with technical detail underneath. Review a sample report with Codility to confirm that your recruiters can interpret the information they need.
External-client sharing requires confirmation for your account and workflow.
No. Your recruitment team makes the submission decision after reviewing the assessment evidence.
Yes, when you enable the AI Assistant. The setting applies per assessment, and every interaction is captured as reviewable AI activity when enabled.
Codility connects with platforms, including Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday and SmartRecruiters. Confirm support for your agency’s system and required workflows during the walkthrough.
Bring one client requisition to the walkthrough
Codility will show you a relevant engineering task and its candidate report. Your team can review the assessment and discuss the agency setup it needs.
